title: Supporting weight-loss maintenance after GLP-1 therapy
official: Post-programme behavioural support for weight-loss maintenance following specialist weight management services: a randomised controlled trial
summary:
Background and study aims
Weight loss medications can help people lose weight, but many people find it difficult to maintain their weight loss after stopping treatment. Weight regain is common, and more research is needed to understand how best to support people during this transition.

This study aims to find out whether a 12-month weight maintenance support programme can help people maintain their weight loss after stopping weight loss medication. The programme provides additional health coaching, educational content and support if participants begin to regain weight.

The study will compare this additional support with the usual support available through the Second Nature app to find out whether it helps people maintain their weight loss.

Who can participate?
Healthy adults may be able to take part if they are participating in the Specialist Weight Management Programme delivered by Second Nature, are approaching the end of their programme and have lost at least 5% of their starting body weight during the programme.

What does the study involve?
Eligible participants will be invited to take part before completing their programme. Participation is voluntary and choosing not to take part will not affect the care or support they receive.

Participants will take part in the study for 12 months. At the start of the study, they will complete online questionnaires and record their weight using digital weighing scales. This will take approximately 30 minutes.

Participants will then be randomly assigned by a computer to one of two groups:
Weight maintenance support group: Participants will continue to have access to the Second Nature app and will also receive monthly group coaching sessions and weekly educational content focused on maintaining weight loss. Their weight measurements will be monitored automatically, and a health coach will contact them to offer additional support if they begin to regain weight.

Comparison group:  Participants will continue to have full access to the Second Nature app, including educational content, recipes and weight-tracking tools, but will not receive the additional weight maintenance support being tested.

All participants will be asked to complete further online questionnaires and record their weight at 6 and 12 months. These will take approximately 20 minutes each time. The questionnaires will ask about eating behaviours, physical activity, quality of life, mood and wellbeing, and work productivity. With participants' consent, relevant information already collected through their Second Nature programme will also be used in the research.

Some participants receiving the additional support will also be invited to take part in an optional video interview at around 6 months. This will last up to 50 minutes and will explore their experiences of the programme.

Participants will receive a £20 voucher for completing the questionnaires at 6 months and another £20 voucher at 12 months. Those who complete an optional interview will receive an additional £25 voucher.

All participants will retain access to the Second Nature app after the study ends.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants receiving the additional support may find it helpful for maintaining their weight loss after stopping medication, although there is no guarantee that they will benefit personally. The study may help researchers understand how to better support people after weight loss medication and improve weight management programmes in the future.

There are no additional medications or medical procedures involved in this study. However, some participants may find questions about their weight, eating habits or mental health uncomfortable. Participants receiving the additional support will also need to spend time engaging with educational content and coaching sessions.

Stopping weight loss medication can be associated with increased hunger, changes in appetite and weight regain. These changes may occur regardless of whether someone takes part in the study.

If questionnaire responses suggest that a participant may need additional mental health support, a member of the research team will contact them. Where there are serious concerns about someone's safety, the research team may need to contact an appropriate healthcare professional.

Participation is voluntary, and participants can withdraw at any time without affecting their usual care or support.

Where is the study run from?
The study is organised and managed by Second Nature, which delivers the Specialist Weight Management Programme. Study activities, including questionnaires, weight monitoring, coaching sessions and optional interviews, will take place remotely through online platforms and the Second Nature app.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
The study will begin recruitment in March 2027, with the first participant starting in April 2027. Recruitment will end in December 2027, with 12-month follow-up concluding by December 2028.

 Who is funding the study?
The study is sponsored and funded by Second Nature, the organisation providing the weight management programme.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Rachel Hall, Chief Investigator and Principal Doctor at Second Nature, rachel@secondnature.io

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.	Adults aged 18 years or over who have completed in the 2-year Second Nature Specialist Weight Management Programme 
2.	Lost ≥5% of body weight from the start of the Specialist Weight Management Programme
3.	Able and willing to provide written informed consent for participation
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Unable to understand the study materials and interventions
2.	Currently following another weight loss programme (defined as a structured, prescribed and monitored programme and not a self-directed weight loss attempt) 
3.	Actively having treatment for an eating disorder in last 12 months
4.	Diagnosis of hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, or thyroid surgery in the last 3 months
5.	Pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant during the course of the study
6.	History of bariatric surgery, including gastric banding
7.	Currently using insulin therapy
8.	Proliferative diabetic retinopathy, or maculopathy.
9.	Recent myocardial infarction or stroke (<3 months)
10.	Renal failure (chronic kidney disease stage 4 or 5)
11.	Current active treatment for cancer (other than skin cancer treated with curative intent by local treatment only or prostate or breast cancer on hormonal treatment only)
12.	Recent self harm (< 3 months) or recent suicide attempt (< 12 months)
